text: How we read. Every row of both tables was copied from the page images (400–600 dpi); OCR is not used: it confuses $\bullet$ with $\circ$ and loses columns. The reading is kept in the repository as text, a line per printed row (metalibrary/toda03, the format is in toda2003.py), and the groups in the cells are derived from it by the program. The table of §5.6 gives whole groups (alpha families included), the table of §6.5 gives them modulo the unstable alpha families (mod A); in the $S^3$ column above we added $A$ back, in the other columns of §6.5 we did not: that has not been done for them, and the grid of §6.5 below is mod A, as in Toda.
The whole text of §5 (with the diagrams and the table of §5.6 in Toda's notation) is on a page of its own: §5 of the paper.

Toda's notation (§5.2): $\bullet\cong\mathbf Z/3$, $\circ\cong\mathbf Z/9$, $\triangleright\cong\mathbf Z/27$; between neighbouring spheres the double suspension $E^2$: “$=$” is a bijection, “$\to$” is non-trivial and not a bijection ($\bullet\to\circ$, $\circ\to\triangleright$ injective, $\circ\to\bullet$, $\triangleright\to\circ$ surjective, $\circ\to\circ$, $\triangleright\to\triangleright$ multiplication by $p$); “$=\langle x\rangle$”: the same group from there on up to the stable one, $x$ the stable generator. A row that ends without “$=\langle\cdot\rangle$” goes to zero on the next sphere. Summands written under each other are separate summands.
PDF pages 67–68 (printed 60–61). There are no rows for $k=1,2,4,5,8,9,12,25$: the groups are zero there.
A cell holds the group: $9\cdot3^2$ means $\mathbf Z/9\oplus(\mathbf Z/3)^2$, empty means zero. The last column is the stable group.
